title: Dark matter and dark energy
examples: How do scientists measure the gravity from things we cannot see?
What is the difference between dark matter and dark energy?
If the universe is expanding, what is causing the acceleration?

explain.say: We know some things in space are invisible to us.
The effect of this unseen mass is called dark matter.
Galaxies spin much faster than visible matter suggests.
This suggests there is a large amount of unseen mass present.
Next, we look at the universe's overall expansion rate.
This speeding up expansion is driven by dark energy.

faq.q: How do we know dark matter exists if we cannot see it?
faq.a: We know it exists because of its gravitational effects on visible objects like galaxies.
asks: What is the evidence for dark matter?
How does dark matter affect stars?

faq.q: Is dark energy the same thing as dark matter?
faq.a: No, they are different concepts. Dark matter provides extra gravity, while dark energy pushes things apart.
asks: Are dark matter and dark energy related?
What is the difference between the two?

faq.q: What is the universe expanding because of?
faq.a: The expansion is accelerating because of a mysterious force called dark energy.
asks: Why is the universe speeding up?

faq.q: How much of the universe is dark matter?
faq.a: Scientists estimate that dark matter makes up about twenty-seven percent of the total mass-energy.
asks: Is dark matter more or less than regular matter?

faq.q: Can we detect dark matter directly in a lab?
faq.a: Currently, we have not directly detected dark matter particles in a laboratory setting.
asks: Is there a way to catch dark matter?
What experiments look for dark matter?

facts: Dark matter does not emit, absorb, or reflect light.
Dark energy is thought to be a property of space itself.
The combination of dark matter and dark energy dominates the universe's composition.
The discovery of accelerated expansion was a major finding in modern cosmology.

quiz.say: What is the primary evidence used to infer the existence of dark matter?

options.show: The observed speed of stars in a galaxy
options.say: The observed speed of stars in a galaxy

options.show: The temperature of the cosmic microwave background
options.say: The temperature of the cosmic microwave background

options.show: The gravitational pull of visible stars
options.say: The gravitational pull of visible stars

quiz.why: The stars move too fast based only on visible matter, requiring extra unseen mass.

wrong.1: Redshift measures expansion, not the missing mass causing rotational speed differences.
wrong.2: This measures the early universe's cooling, not the current gravitational imbalance.
wrong.3: This only accounts for the known matter, ignoring the required extra pull.

quiz.say: What force is responsible for the universe's accelerating expansion?
quiz.why: Dark energy acts like a repulsive force inherent to space itself.

wrong.1: Gravity is an attractive force, pulling matter inward, which slows expansion.
wrong.2: Dark matter contributes extra gravity, which would slow down the expansion.
wrong.3: This force is too weak and localized to affect the entire cosmos.

quiz.say: If the universe were only made of visible matter, how would its expansion behave?

options.show: It would expand at a constant rate
options.say: It would expand at a constant rate

options.show: It would speed up faster than observed
options.say: It would speed up faster than observed

options.show: It would slow down over time
options.say: It would slow down over time

quiz.why: Gravity from all matter pulls everything together, resisting expansion.

wrong.0: Constant expansion would imply no opposing forces like gravity.
wrong.1: Stopping requires a perfect balance, which is not currently observed.
wrong.2: The current evidence points to an accelerating, not an excessively fast, rate.
